newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica tobacco shares hacked by US firm admission.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica tobacco shares hacked by US firm admission.

text.p: South African tobacco companies Rembrandt and Richemont were buffetted on Monday by industry worries over U.S. firm Liggett's cooperation with anti-tobacco plaintiffs, dealers said.
Tobacco group Liggett last week released sensitive documents to U.S. states suing the tobacco industry which, among other admissions, said smoking damages health and is addictive.

The admissions are expected to have far-reaching legal effects, including boosting the U.S. Justice Department's criminal probe of cigarette companies and are seen having repercussions for tobacco companies worldwide.
Rembrandt and Richemont were respectively the second and third largest traders by value on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange by 0945 GMT.
Rembrandt had lost 45 cents to 45.05 rand in a traded volume of 278,700 shares for value 12.5 million rand.
Richemont Securities had shed 75 cents or over one percent to 58.75 rand with 241,400 shares having changed hands for value 14.2 million rand.
"We could see big selling in Rembrandt which will come under pressure because of that (Liggett news)," one dealer said.
"It ties in with a current market trend that will see continued pressure for tobacco stocks," he added.

The companies merged their tobacco interests in October 1995 to form Luxembourg-incorporated company Rothmans International Holdings. Richemont owns two thirds of Rothmans International and Rembrandt one third.
